rules.statement: When one endpoint replaces a sequence of existing operations (such as create-then-delete), authorize the caller for every operation it replaces, so the combined endpoint grants nothing the separate calls would not.
rules.why: Otherwise the combined endpoint becomes a way to get around the authorization of the individual operations.
rules.check: Look for a new composite or convenience endpoint that checks only one permission, or a new permission, when the underlying operations each have their own authorization checks.

rules.statement: When a credential is replaced, add the new one and remove the old one in a single unit of work (one save), so the owning entity never ends up with both or with neither.
rules.why: Doing it in two steps means a failure between them leaves the old credential still accepted, or leaves no credential at all.
rules.check: Look for rotation or replacement code that saves the new entity and deletes the old one in separate SaveChanges or transactions, or across separate calls.

rules.statement: Return generated secret material only in the response to the request that creates it, and keep it out of audit records, logs and every later read.
rules.why: Secret material is revealed once on create, and the audit trail records the creation and deletion without the material.
rules.check: Look for generated secret bytes or values written to audit events, logs, or GET/list responses, or for a rotate or create path whose response does not carry the newly generated material.

rules.statement: When an operation acts on an existing resource and the client sends an `If-Match` header, check it against the concurrency token of the resource being modified or removed, and reject the request if they do not match.
rules.why: This keeps optimistic concurrency working on combined operations, the same way it does on the individual update and delete calls.
rules.check: Look for endpoints that modify or delete an existing resource and either ignore `If-Match` or compare it against the wrong entity's token.

rules.statement: Do not have the server generate or hold replacement private key material for an asymmetric key the client owns (imported, or published at its `jwks_uri`); reject such server-side rotation with `400` and let the client import the new key and delete the old one.
rules.why: The server would end up holding the private key of a credential the client owns, and it has no material to replace that key with.
rules.check: Look for rotation or regeneration code that creates key pairs for client-owned signing or encryption keys, or that accepts asymmetric key types without returning a 400.
